task.description: Diagnose queue task 274 / ISS-0274 (GH#542): web/tsconfig.json is solution-style ('files': [] plus references-only), making 'npm run type-check' (tsc --noEmit against the root config) a no-op that compiles zero files and always passes regardless of real type errors in the referenced project configs.
acceptance_criteria: Step 0.5 registry lookup performed and result stated
Reproduced directly with real command output (or explicit explanation why not runnable, plus evidence from source instead)
Root cause traced to the specific config field and invocation mismatch
Diagnosis written into result.summary; do NOT implement the fix; next_action names CODE-DESIGNER

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): searched docs/issues/*.yaml for prior resolved entries mentioning tsconfig/type-check/solution-style. One textual match, docs/issues/ISS-0046.yaml, is unrelated (an Elixir mix compile --warnings-as-errors struct-update type-inference warning in lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, not a frontend tsconfig issue) -- ruled out. No prior resolved entry matches ISS-0274's symptoms. This is a first occurrence, not a recurrence.

STEP 1 (diagnose): Reproduced directly on this branch (feature/WF03-ISS0274-20260822), npm/npx are runnable in this environment.

Evidence read from source: web/tsconfig.json is exactly:
```
{
  "files": [],
  "references": [
    { "path": "./tsconfig.app.json" },
    { "path": "./tsconfig.node.json" }
  ]
}
```
This is TypeScript's documented 'solution style' root config -- an empty file list plus project references only, meant to be driven exclusively by 'tsc -b' (build mode), never by a plain 'tsc' invocation. web/package.json's type-check script (line 10) is: `"type-check": "tsc --noEmit"` -- a plain (non -b) tsc invocation with no explicit project argument, so it resolves the root web/tsconfig.json.

Direct reproduction: ran `npm run type-check` in web/ -- output is just the npm script banner ('> letflow-web@0.1.0 type-check' / '> tsc --noEmit'), no diagnostics, exit code 0 (confirmed separately via `npm run type-check; echo EXIT:$?` -> EXIT:0). To prove this is a zero-file no-op rather than a real clean pass, ran `npx tsc --noEmit --listFiles` in the same directory: output is completely empty (0 lines) -- tsc compiled and type-checked NO files at all under the root config, because 'files': [] gives it nothing to check and a plain (non -b) tsc invocation does not descend into 'references' automatically. Contrast: ran `npx tsc -b tsconfig.json --dry`, which reports 'A non-dry build would build project .../tsconfig.app.json' and '.../tsconfig.node.json' -- i.e. build (-b) mode is the invocation that actually walks the referenced projects' real source files (src/** via tsconfig.app.json's "include": ["src"], and vite.config.ts via tsconfig.node.json's "include": ["vite.config.ts"]). A real `npx tsc -b tsconfig.json` run (non-dry) exited 0 with no output, meaning the codebase currently has no type errors under the referenced projects -- consistent with REQ-115/REVIEWER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR's finding that the gate itself is a no-op, not that it happens to be passing a real check.

ROOT CAUSE: web/tsconfig.json's 'files': [] (solution-style, references-only) field combined with web/package.json's type-check script invoking plain `tsc --noEmit` with no '-b' flag and no explicit project file. A solution-style root tsconfig is only meaningful to tsc in build mode ('tsc -b'); invoked any other way, tsc resolves the root config, sees an empty file list and no 'include', and has zero files to type-check -- it exits 0 unconditionally, independent of any real type errors in tsconfig.app.json's or tsconfig.node.json's projects (which DO have real 'include' globs and are where all actual application/vite-config source lives). This is a pure invocation/config mismatch, not a bug in tsconfig.app.json or tsconfig.node.json themselves -- both of those referenced configs are otherwise correctly formed (each has 'noEmit': true already set, each has a real 'include').

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE: web/package.json's "type-check" script (currently `tsc --noEmit`) needs to invoke tsc in a way that actually walks both referenced projects, e.g. `tsc -b tsconfig.json` (or equivalently `tsc -b tsconfig.app.json tsconfig.node.json`, or bare `tsc -b` since tsconfig.json is the default project file and already declares both references). Because both tsconfig.app.json and tsconfig.node.json already set "noEmit": true in their own compilerOptions, '-b' mode will type-check without writing output -- no extra '--noEmit' flag is needed or applicable to '-b' mode (tsc -b does not accept '--noEmit' as a per-invocation override the way non-build mode does; emit is controlled by each project's own noEmit setting, which is already correct here). Note web/package.json's existing "build" script (line 8) already correctly uses `tsc -b && vite build` -- the fix should make "type-check" consistent with that established pattern rather than inventing a new one. CODE-DESIGNER should also consider whether '-b' mode's incremental build-info caching (.tsbuildinfo files) could mask a real error on a second run without a clean rebuild (i.e. whether '--force' or a cache-clear step is needed for a CI fail-fast gate to be reliable across multiple invocations) -- I did not test repeated invocations against a deliberately broken file, so this is flagged as an open design question rather than a confirmed finding.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design: change web/package.json's "type-check" script from `tsc --noEmit` to a build-mode invocation that actually walks tsconfig.app.json and tsconfig.node.json (e.g. `tsc -b tsconfig.json` or `tsc -b`), matching the existing `build` script's `tsc -b && vite build` pattern, and decide whether incremental build-info caching needs a --force/clean step for CI fail-fast reliability. See result.summary above for full reproduction evidence (empty --listFiles output under the current no-op invocation vs. tsc -b --dry actually targeting both referenced projects).
